draftInput._note: The redactor's contract operates on extractor draft output (narrative.*, traction text, provenance source_snippet) — NOT on the raw paste. This fixture is a cross-reference: the redactor's caller (the extractor agent) reads the paste at paste-mosaic-marketplace.txt, emits a draft that quotes the Slack thread inside provenance source_snippets, and at THAT point the redactor walks the draft. T7's test loads the referenced file, runs the agent, and asserts the byType counts below against the resulting draft.

expectedRedactions.values_note: T7 reads the referenced file at test time and asserts the email values found there — the literal email strings are NOT inlined in this fixture file so the grep gate (every @-domain in .example/.test/.invalid) holds. The mosaic paste authored its addresses against the SLD-form RFC-2606 reserved domains (example.com / example.org / example.net), which the redactor's email regex must accept.

description: The mosaic-marketplace paste already carries 6 unrelated-party PII items in its embedded Slack thread (3 VC emails + 3 VC phones across lines 69 / 72 / 78). The two founders (Sofia Park / Hassan Bakr) have no contact info in the paste, so no founder-self preservation is exercised here — only the unrelated-party scrub. The expectedRedactions email values are intentionally NOT inlined in this fixture file (the referenced file authors them against the SLD-form RFC-2606 reserved domains, which would fail this file's grep gate that pins every email TLD to .example/.test/.invalid). The T7 test loads the referenced file at test time and asserts the email count and shape against the resulting redacted draft. The narrative blob is held by reference so this file does not duplicate the mosaic paste.
rationale: Real-world precedent: the redactor's contract is anchored to the same paste the extractor unit tests already operate on. Proves end-to-end consistency between extractor + redactor.
